Cross-project rules live in `rules/` (distributed from here, not about this repo).  ## Shell: target bash 3.2 (IMPORTANT)  **Both machines run macOS system bash 3.2.57; there is no bash 4+ on `PATH`** (validated 2026-07-26). Everything here — `scripts/`, `hooks/`, `install.sh`, `benchmarks/` — executes under it. Unavailable, each failing at *runtime* rather than parse time:
| Feature | bash 4+ only | Use instead | |---|---|---| | `mapfile` / `readarray` | 4.0 | `while IFS= read -r x; do arr+=("$x"); done < <(cmd)` | | `local -n` / `declare -n` namerefs | 4.3 | Echo results on stdout; caller reads into an array | | Associative arrays `declare -A` | 4.0 | Parallel indexed arrays, `case`, or `jq` | | `${var,,}` / `${var^^}` | 4.0 | `tr 'A-Z' 'a-z'` | | `&>>`, `|&` | 4.0 | `>>file 2>&1`, `2>&1 |` |  **`bash -n` does not catch these** — it parses fine and dies on execution (2026-07 #219: passed every [redacted-host] check, died on the Mini). Run the actual script, prefer both machines.
macOS userland, not GNU:  - **No `timeout`/`gtimeout`** without coreutils. Portable: `perl -e 'alarm shift @ARGV; exec @ARGV' <secs> <cmd...>`. - **`date +%s%3N` is GNU-only.** Milliseconds: `python3 -c 'import time; print(int(time.time()*1000))'`. - **BSD `sed -i` requires an argument**: `sed -i.bak … && rm -f file.bak`, or prefer `python3`. - **`python3 - <<'PY'` consumes stdin for the PROGRAM** — piped data never reaches `sys.stdin.read()` (returns `""`, silently). Pass the program with `-c` and keep data on stdin (2026-08-09, [[redacted-project]#386]([redacted-url])). - **`claude -p` in a script/heredoc EATS THE REST OF THE SCRIPT as prompt stdin** — later lines silently never execute. Always `claude -p "…" < /dev/null` (2026-07-28, left invalid JSON in a live settings.json on [redacted-host]). - **An env assignment binds to the command it prefixes, not the far side of a pipe.** `VAR=x cmd | python3 -c '…'` leaves the python unset; put the assignment on the reading process (2026-08-12, `resume-work.sh`). - **Backticks inside a double-quoted `record-cli`/`slack` body are command substitution** — spans silently replaced by empty output, exit 0. Use single [redacted-project] or `--body-file` (2026-08-16, repaired via `record-cli api PATCH`). - **A malformed `settings.json` silently disables EVERY setting in it** — no error; hooks just stop firing. Writers must validate JSON and write atomically (tempfile + `os.replace`). Hooks mysteriously dead → JSON-lint the file first.
- **`set -o pipefail` + `grep` for a key that may be absent kills the script** — grep exits 1 on no match and pipefail makes the whole pipeline fatal. Use `sed -n 's/…/p'` or append `|| true` (2026-08-23, [[redacted-project]#615]([redacted-url]): [redacted-host]'s unattended install died mid-block on a missing config.toml key). - **A hook that emits JSON must build it with an encoder, never a heredoc** — a heredoc with `${VAR}` interpolated into a JSON string value breaks the moment a variable contains a newline, a quote, or a backslash. Build the text plainly and encode once (`jq -n --arg`, or `python3 -c 'json.dump(...)'`); assert on the DECODED string, not just valid-JSON. Detail: `docs/claude-md-gotcha-hooks-and-test-fixtures.md`. - **A `factory.*` module invoked from bash must import stdlib only** — the ops scripts call bare `python3`, where `pydantic` and `python-dotenv` are NOT installed (validated 2026-09-01). `factory.tracer`/`envelopes`/`utils` pull in both, so a shell-invoked module must stay clear of them; `yaml_scalar` (#824) and `run_trace` (#861) are the pattern. Invisible in the `uv`-run Python suite — pin it with a subprocess test that imports the module with those names poisoned (pattern: `tests/test_run_trace.py::test_cli_imports_without_third_party_dependencies`). - **Never resolve a repo from `basename(cwd)` and a hardcoded map** — the map drifts silently and the catch-all arm aims work at the wrong repo. `[redacted-path]]-ios` matched no arm in `session-tracker.sh`, so every [redacted-project] session was told to file its tickets in [redacted-project]. Derive from `git remote get-url origin`; when there is no remote, emit nothing rather than defaulting (2026-08-30, #712). - **`git rev-parse --show-toplevel` names the BRANCH DIRECTORY inside a linked worktree**, not the repo — `.worktrees/234-devops-two-tier` resolves to itself. Use `--git-common-dir` and take its parent when you want the repo's identity (2026-08-30, #712). - **Session type is detectable in a hook: `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT` is `cli` interactively and `sdk-cli` under `claude -p`** (validated 2.1.251), and `agent_id` on the hook payload marks a subagent. Gate cost-bearing injection on both. EXCLUDE known-headless values rather than allow-listing `cli` — an IDE, desktop, or future entrypoint would otherwise silently lose the injection, which is the invisible failure (2026-08-30, #712). - **Tests that run `install.sh` must sandbox a COPY of the repo (`cp -R` + strip `.git`), not just `HOME`** — generation writes into `$DOTFILES_DIR`, and a worktree run resolves to main. Pattern: `tests/test-codex-agent-install.sh` (2026-08-23, #615 code review: the imports test was rewriting main's tracked AGENTS.md and leaving it 0600). - **Claude Code does not expand `$HOME` in settings.json's `env` block.** A literal `$HOME/.local/bin` in `env.PATH` ships to every machine unexpanded, so `claude` and `[redacted-path]` vanish from every tool shell, hook, and subagent. install.sh expands it at merge time; the tracked source keeps `$HOME` because [redacted-host]'s automation account is `claude` (2026-09-01, [[redacted-project]#858]([redacted-url])). - **Codex reads only the first 32 KiB of an AGENTS.md, silently** — no warning, no truncation marker (validated 2026-09-01 by `codex exec` in [redacted-project]: a fact at byte 32,700 is recalled, one past 32,768 is not). **Per-file, not cumulative, for the global `CODEX_HOME/AGENTS.md` + cwd `AGENTS.md` pair** (validated 2026-09-24, #875: a ~31.9 KiB global file plus a small cwd file; a marker at cumulative offset >36 KiB was still recalled). **Open question: the `[redacted-path]` tier is unvalidated.** The probe was inconclusive: a synthetic non-git ancestor `AGENTS.md` was not recalled even at byte 0, so Codex may not read that file at all. Every Codex-consumed surface must independently stay under 32 KiB; assertions: `tests/ops/test-agents-md-byte-ceiling.sh` (#875; follow-on to [[redacted-project]#857]([redacted-url])). - **A parser for another tool's output must be pinned against that tool's REAL output, captured into a fixture — a hand-written sample is invented test data and hides format drift.** A fail-closed gate whose broken output is identical to its healthy output cannot be caught by reading its report. Capture the real thing into a fixture, assert an exact count against it, and assert the *negative* state word too. Detail: `docs/claude-md-gotcha-hooks-and-test-fixtures.md`.
- **A commit subject beginning `fix: #N` (or `fixes: #N`, `closes: #N`) auto-closes issue N when it reaches main** — GitHub's close-keyword match tolerates the colon. The close bypasses `close-issue.sh`, so the issue ends up closed with its `status/*` label still on it and its deployed-verification never runs. Write `Refs [redacted-person]/<repo>#N` in the body and keep the ticket number out of a `fix:`-prefixed subject (2026-09-03, #898 closed itself on merge `[redacted-commit]`; reopened by hand). - **A worktree agent's Playwright output lands in the MAIN checkout.** The Playwright tools write relative to their own cwd, not the agent's worktree, so screenshots and `.playwright-mcp/` snapshots appear as untracked files in the shared main tree. A path outside the checkout is not an option: from a session started in the main checkout the tool refused the scratchpad with `File access denied … outside allowed roots` (2026-10-01, [[redacted-project]#604]([redacted-url])). Save under `.playwright-mcp/` and delete the files you created before finishing (2026-09-02, #890 gen). - **`cmd | tail -1` (or any pipe) replaces the command's exit code with the pipe's.** A red pytest piped through `tail` reads as success to `&&`, and a chained `git push` then lands a failing tree on main — it did once on 2026-09-02 (#609 merge). Capture the code first: `cmd > log 2>&1; rc=$?; tail -1 log`, then branch on `$rc`. - **A test that drives a job harness (`ops/jobs/*/check.sh`) must stub EVERY external effect the harness can reach, senders included — stubbing only the state dirs is the leak.** When adding a live-state guard to a job, enumerate its effect channels (state dirs, Slack, record-cli, launchd), not just its data dirs. Detail: `docs/claude-md-gotcha-hooks-and-test-fixtures.md`. - **A blanket search-and-replace in a shell test must stop at heredoc boundaries.** A quoted heredoc (`<<'SH'`) that generates a stub is a separate runtime scope — a variable from the test's top level does not exist inside it, so a global rename can silently break a heredoc-generated stub instead of updating it (2026-09-04, `[redacted-commit]` in `tests/test-codex-hook-install.sh`). Check each replace site against the nearest heredoc opener before running. - **A job's `repo enabled:` line in its config is not the off switch.** `install.sh` preserves the box's existing value for `enabled`, so editing the tracked config has no effect on a box that already installed it. Use `scripts/ops/jobs.sh disable <job>` to change the running state (2026-09-21, session [redacted-commit]). [[redacted-project]#1396]([redacted-url]) keeps that behavior and makes it visible: every install, including `--dry-run`, reports a repo-versus-effective mismatch as a `CONFLICT` line and an `enabled_conflicts` record in `install-ops.status.json` (contract: `ops/jobs/ENABLED.md`). - **Two `record-cli issue create` calls in one Bash command trip `require-triage-labels`** ("exactly one model/"): the hook reads the whole command text and sees both label sets. One create per Bash call (2026-09-02, #705 round). - **zsh reads `$c:agents/...` as a history modifier on `$c`**, not as the variable followed by a colon. Write `${c}:path` when a variable is immediately followed by `:` (2026-09-02). - **Config symlinked into place from this repo is edited at the source, then re-verified live.** A CLI that writes through the symlink (`claude mcp remove`) reads back clean and is then reverted by the tracked file. Edit the [redacted-identity] source, run `install.sh` if it manages the link, and make the live check (`claude mcp get <name>`) the last step before reporting done (an `idb` MCP removal was reported done and came back). - **Unattended `claude -p` from launchd has its own failure modes**: token-file auth instead of the keychain, launchd's PATH, silent degradation behind try/except, a hang when nested in a session, prefix-matched Bash permissions, and locking without `flock`. Playbook: `docs/headless-claude-p-launchd.md`.
 ## install.sh runs no runtime tests (IMPORTANT)  `install.sh` performs the [redacted-identity] install only (symlinks, the settings.json merge, hook and generated rules/AGENTS.md surfaces) and does **not** run the factory pytest suite as an install precondition (#906) — do not reintroduce one; `tests/test-codex-agent-install.sh` asserts the gate stays out. The governor merge gate runs the factory suite at merge (#916). **That gate covers factory merges only.** For every merge you do by hand, the suite run IS the gate: `cd factory && uv run pytest -q` on the MERGED tree (temp worktree on `origin/main`, `merge --no-ff`, gate, push), exit code captured, before the push. Full history: `docs/claude-md-gotcha-install-merge-gate.md`.
 **A merge whose whole diff is under `docs/` or `skills/` skips the suite** ([redacted-person] 2026-10-02, [[redacted-project]#604]([redacted-url]): a one-file spec merge cost a 21-minute run; `skills/` added by [redacted-person] 2026-10-06, since the factory suite does not execute skill text). Confirm the diff with `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD`. Some tests read files under `docs/` and `skills/` (for example `tests/ops/test-registry-views.sh` checks issue-workflow's generated tables), so check each changed path with `git grep -l -- <path> factory/tests tests`: no hit means no gate, and a hit means run only the test files it names.  **A commit that touches `factory/src` needs its [redacted-project] port-record entry merged first** (`docs/migration/1143/runtime-port-record-v1.json` in [redacted-project]; classes in `runtime-drift-audit.md` beside it). `factory/tests/test_runtime_port_record.py` reads that record from the sibling [redacted-project] checkout and fails every [redacted-project] merge gate until the commit has an entry, so merge the entry to [redacted-project] before or with the [redacted-identity] merge, and pull the [redacted-project] checkout. A generated file counts (`workflow_catalog_generated.py`). Overriding the hand-merge suite run also skips this check (2026-10-08, [[redacted-project]#1696]([redacted-url]): `[redacted-commit]` merged without an entry and turned main red for every session).  ## A running launchd daemon keeps its old code until restart (IMPORTANT)  Merging a `factory/` change to main does NOT make it live on a box that runs a persistent factory daemon (`com.[redacted-person].slack-listener`, `com.[redacted-person].slack-session-manager`) until it is restarted. Deploy in order: (1) `git -C [redacted-path]] pull --ff-only origin
main`, (2) `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/<label>`. Verify the daemon's log after — a **green suite is not deployed-verification** for daemon code. Full history: `docs/claude-md-gotcha-install-merge-gate.md`.  ## Migrate shell → Python when you touch it — task runner (IMPORTANT)  Standing order for every agent on the runtime (`factory/`, `ops/jobs/`, `scripts/ops/`), [redacted-person] 2026-08-20: when you must **edit** a runtime shell script or **add a dependency** on one, look at migrating it to typed, tested `factory.*` Python first (#585/#591 ported the core). The bar is "migrate unless there's a reason not to". When Python needs a shell script's behavior, **port the logic in — never shell out to it** (dispatch-codex.sh → governor is the worked example).  ## Writing hooks (IMPORTANT)
Before writing or editing anything in `hooks/`, read **`docs/hook-authoring.md`** — observability scoping, fail-open, matcher ownership, throttle-vs-backstop flags, subject-vs-ambient state, label-vocabulary derivation, and the `--repo` requirement on `record-cli issue create`.  ## No production data inside git working trees (IMPORTANT — standing order, [redacted-person] 2026-09-01)  Runtime/production state never lives inside a git checkout. When you SEE any production state polluting a working tree — DBs, caches, run dirs, logs — flag it and file a migration ticket; when you ADD a state path, put it under `$DATA_HOME/state/` (or `$FACTORY_*`/`ADMIN_*` env-overridable equivalents), resolved through the configured root, never under the repo and never as a hardcoded `[redacted-path]` literal (rules/dev.md §Runtime paths). Case history: `docs/claude-md-gotcha-state-and-env-defaults.md`.
 ## Architecture map — `docs/architecture/`  `docs/architecture/runtime.html` is this repo's runtime architecture: how install.sh composes config into `[redacted-path]` and `[redacted-path]` for agent sessions and hooks, and the factory job runtime on the Minis (scheduler, run-check.sh, governor, worker sessions, merge runner). Each box links to the file and lines it came from. `runtime.architecture.json` is its source, pinned to one commit in `meta.repository.revision`. The Slack plane, `run-job.sh` model jobs, and verdict/suite runners are not on this map.  Maps in this folder:  - `runtime.html` (architecture): the runtime map described above. - `ticket-lifecycle.html` (lifecycle): a ticket's status states and the label gates enforced on each transition (create, execute, dispatch route, close), with doc-vs-code findings. - `dev-execute.html` (workflow): one ticket's gen → native review → eval rounds, admission, verdict and merge, with what is enforced in code versus prose only.
 - Read the map before structural work, then confirm against the code. It is correct only as of its pinned commit. - When a change moves a box or an edge, regenerate it with the `archify` skill: from `docs/architecture/`, run `node [redacted-path] finalize architecture runtime.architecture.json runtime.html --repo-root <repo> --quality showcase --json`, then commit the JSON and the HTML only.  Introduced by [[redacted-project]#1589]([redacted-url]).  ## Where things live  - `rules/` — the always-loaded rules sources (`core.md` cross-tool, `claude.md` Claude-harness, `dev.md` dev workflow, `practices/` tier-tagged) + generated surfaces via install.sh. See `docs/rules-rework/rulebook.md` and `docs/rules-rework/composition-flow.html`. - `benchmarks/` — model A/B harness (#219); read its README before adding a suite.
- `.github/suites.json` — the only list of test suites and the CI gate that runs each ([[redacted-project]#1706]([redacted-url])). Read it before proposing any suite or merge-gate change (2026-10-08: a gate option was offered for `tests/test-*.sh`, which its `repo-shell` suite already ran). - `ops/config/registry.yaml` — **the single source for which projects and repos are in the issue lifecycle** (#866). `machine-map.yaml` and the `issue-workflow` scope table are GENERATED from it by `scripts/ops/gen-registry-views.py`; `install.sh` regenerates them. Edit the registry, never a generated view. `runtime: none` marks a real project the runtime never dispatches; `project_reserved` holds the `project/*` values that are not projects (`tbd`, `no-project`) and must never reach machine-map. - `skills/`, `agents/`, `hooks/`, `commands/` — symlinked into `[redacted-path]` by `install.sh`. **A new or renamed skill is invisible until `install.sh` runs**, from the main checkout only (see `rules/dev.md`). - `hosts/[redacted-host]/iterm2/` — [redacted-host]-only iTerm2 profiles; **read `hosts/[redacted-host]/iterm2/README.md` before editing** (two silent failure modes). - `AGENTS.md` (repo root) — GENERATED (this file only) for Codex; edit this file, then run `install.sh`. Core rules load separately from the generated `[redacted-path]` (source: `rules/core.md`).  ## A live-path env default is a hidden test input (IMPORTANT)  Any `_env()` / `os.environ` default that resolves to a **live** path — a database, a cache, a state directory — is read by every test that does not override it, so the test suite
silently takes the developer's machine as an input. When you add such a default, add a matching autouse guard in `factory/tests/conftest.py` in the same change (it already isolates `TWO_TIER_BOARD_CACHE`, `FACTORY_DB`, `SWEEP_FACTORY_DB`); per-test discipline is not the mechanism, the fixture is. Case history: `docs/claude-md-gotcha-state-and-env-defaults.md`.  ## Install guards keyed on another installer's artifact only fire in one order (IMPORTANT)  When [redacted-identity] and an external package (research-tools) both want to create the same link, a guard that tests **the artifact the other installer creates** is silently order-dependent: it fires where that installer ran first, and does nothing where it
did not. Key the guard on something true in **both** orders — typically the input you already own. Generalization: **a package that owns a skill's Claude link owns its Codex link too.** When onboarding a new external package, check every guard in the mirror path for this ordering assumption rather than counting guard sites. Case history: `docs/claude-md-gotcha-state-and-env-defaults.md`.  ## publish-doc.sh on [redacted-host]: pass the serve-root (IMPORTANT)  On [redacted-host] always pass `--serve-root [redacted-path] --out-subdir docs` — the default serve-root lands outside the served tree and 404s silently. Verify with `curl -4 -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" <url>` before sharing (the `-4` is required — a tailscale IPv4 literal can resolve to an IPv6 address and time out, returning `000` for a healthy server; forcing IPv4 is always safe for these literals); the server binds the tailscale IP only. Full detail: `[redacted-path]]/context/build-host-operations.md`.
